findings.issue_text: UsernameForm calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() but only a one-argument overload exists in UsernamePasswordForm; UsernameForm doesn't inherit it and holds no webauthnAuth field, likely causing a compile break or an inconsistent 'passkeys enabled' notion using no realm context, breaking the skip-to-IDP re-auth path

The isConditionalPasskeysEnabled predicate is duplicated in UsernameForm and UsernamePasswordForm with diverging signatures; should be hoisted into AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator or AuthenticatorUtils so future changes don't need to be made in two classes

The webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test never asserts a LOGIN_ERROR event after a wrong-password login before events.clear(), so a regression in the failed login error path would go undetected

Realm passkeys policy alone forces the username form for users with no passkey credential: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() never checks whether the re-authenticating user owns a webauthn credential, silently dropping the auto-skip fast path for credential-less users in passkeys-enabled realms, and no test covers this case

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) fills webauthn form data for users with no webauthn credentials, rendering a passkey button that cannot authenticate and previously-suppressed empty-authenticators branch is now unreachable for the conditional path, with this regression path untested

Linked-broker (IDP) re-authentication escape hatch is silently dropped when passkeys are enabled: the restructured condition skips the hasLinkedBrokers block, forcing broker-linked users through the username/password form with no test coverage

Test assertion in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey can never fail: AssertionError thrown by assertThat(..., nullValue()) is caught by the same catch(Exception) block so fail() never propagates, making the negative test vacuous; should use assertThrows instead

UsernamePasswordForm.java:113-115: webauthnAuth.fillContextForm moved out of the user==null branch and gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) which requires user != null, inverting the condition so first-time unidentified users no longer get WebAuthn form data / passkey UI during initial login

UsernameForm.java:47: username form shown to every user when realm passkeys are enabled, without checking whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey credential, forcing password-only users through a username re-confirmation step with a failing passkey widget

Divergent definitions of 'passkeys enabled' in sibling classes: UsernameForm uses no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() while UsernamePasswordForm uses isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) requiring non-null user, causing drift and inconsistent passkey UI between the two pages

setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only wired into two error paths (badPasswordHandler and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse), not other challenge() error renderings on the re-auth path, so the hidden-username attribute isn't re-applied and the username field reappears inconsistently

Test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys policy instead of testing the enabled-realm + credential-less-user combination, hiding the regression

fillContextForm is now invoked with a non-null user through a code path (else branch of WebAuthnAuthenticator) written for the unidentified-user case, and the else branch may derive the username from login_hint rather than the re-authenticating user, rendering the wrong/blank username
No test covers the enabled-passkeys + identified-user + no-passkey-credential rendering path for fillContextForm

AuthenticatorUtils.java reimplements inline the logic of isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, creating two parsers of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note with no single source of truth, risking silent divergence if the note's semantics change

UsernameForm.java:47 gates skipping the username form on realm-wide isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() rather than on the user actually having a passkey, so password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms get an extra re-auth step
No test in the diff covers re-auth through UsernameForm for a password-only user

WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:63 shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false unconditionally makes the inherited 2FA branch of fillContextForm (authenticator selection list) dead code for all instances, breaking pre-identified-user flows

PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:197-201 silently reverses a previously accepted assertion (NoSuchElementException for the webauth form) to assert the form is present, changing the organizations flow's acceptance criteria without explicit maintainer sign-off

UsernamePasswordForm.java:113/137 inverts the fill condition from 'user not yet selected' to 'user selected', so realms without the WebAuthn passwordless execution in the browser flow silently lose conditional-UI form data on the username/password page
The UsernamePasswordForm coupling change is untested in the configuration without the co-resident WebAuthn execution

PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication test does not assert the username form was rendered, so the regression fixed by the UsernameForm.authenticate change (skip only when !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) is invisible — the test passes green even if the behavior is reverted; same gap exists in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest's same-named test

WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse new error-path branch (setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError on passkey failure) has zero test coverage — no test simulates a failed passkey attempt during re-authentication

PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey never asserts that the username input is hidden and registration is disabled, the two attributes the extracted AuthenticUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError exists to set — if the util silently no-ops the test still passes

PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses an inverted try/catch assertion idiom where assertThat(..., nullValue()) is dead code and non-assertion exceptions (e.g., WebDriverException) are silently swallowed, passing the test without verifying anything — should use assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) instead; the idiom is duplicated twice

Inverted user-presence condition in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() (~113-117): isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, but conditional-UI fillContextForm must run when user == null (fresh login), so passkey autofill/conditional mediation is silently lost on the primary login path
Same inverted gate in challenge() also prevents fillContextForm from being invoked on fresh login

shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator hard-returns false, causing fillContextForm in createErrorResponse to always take the anonymous path even when a user is identified, so the error-challenge page after a failed passkey during 2FA re-auth never shows the authenticator-selection list
Nothing in code or logs distinguishes intentional suppression from lost authenticator list, making the behavior invisible to future maintainers changing error rendering

Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The isConditionalPasskeysEnabled predicate is duplicated in UsernameForm and UsernamePasswordForm with diverging signatures; should be hoisted into AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator or AuthenticatorUtils so future changes don't need to be made in two classes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `UsernamePasswordForm` adding `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` and using it in two places, while `UsernameForm` was changed to call `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg). That indicates the same conceptual predicate is now split across two classes with different signatures/usage patterns, creating a maintainability/architecture concern where future changes to the condition may need to be duplicated and kept consistent. This is not a correctness bug by itself, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded design issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey test never asserts a LOGIN_ERROR event after a wrong-password login before events.clear(), so a regression in the failed login error path would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, the test performs an incorrect-password re-authentication (`loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost"));`) and only asserts the UI error (`Assert.assertEquals("Invalid password.", loginPage.getInputError());`). It then calls `events.clear();` without asserting an expected `EventType.LOGIN_ERROR` / `Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS` event for that failed attempt. This means regressions in the failed-login event/error path during re-authentication could slip by while the UI message still appears.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Realm passkeys policy alone forces the username form for users with no passkey credential: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() never checks whether the re-authenticating user owns a webauthn credential, silently dropping the auto-skip fast path for credential-less users in passkeys-enabled realms, and no test covers this case

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the re-auth fast-path: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now skips the username form only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (so when conditional passkeys are enabled, the form will no longer be auto-skipped even if the user is already known). Also, `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` only checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null` and does not verify the user actually has any WebAuthn/passkey credential. The finding’s specific outcome (“forces the username form for users with no passkey credential”) depends on what `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` in `UsernameForm` considers (not shown in this diff), so it’s not provably a defect from the diff alone. However, the concern is diff-grounded as an unhandled edge-case/UX behavior change, and there is indeed no test added for the case ‘realm passkeys enabled but user has no passkey’; the new test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` covers only `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) fills webauthn form data for users with no webauthn credentials, rendering a passkey button that cannot authenticate and previously-suppressed empty-authenticators branch is now unreachable for the conditional path, with this regression path untested

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, conditional passkeys UI is now populated whenever `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which only checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`—it does **not** verify the identified user actually has any WebAuthn/passwordless credentials. At the same time, `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()`’s previous suppression for identified users with no authenticators (`authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() -> return form`) is now gated by `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that to always return `false`, making the “no authenticators” early-return unreachable for the conditional UI path. This combination can surface a WebAuthn/passkey UI element for a user who cannot authenticate with passkeys. The added tests cover re-authentication *with* passkeys and the case where the realm has passkeys disabled, but do not cover “realm passkeys enabled + user has no passkey” regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Linked-broker (IDP) re-authentication escape hatch is silently dropped when passkeys are enabled: the restructured condition skips the hasLinkedBrokers block, forcing broker-linked users through the username/password form with no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not drop the linked-broker (IDP) behavior. In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` check still exists and would still prevent `context.success()` when executed. The only change is gating the entire “skip form on re-authentication” fast-path behind `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, meaning when passkeys are enabled the form is shown even for non-broker-linked users. That does not specifically “force broker-linked users through username/password” nor does it remove an IDP re-auth option; broker-linked users already would not hit `context.success()` before because `hasLinkedBrokers(context)` would be true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test assertion in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey can never fail: AssertionError thrown by assertThat(..., nullValue()) is caught by the same catch(Exception) block so fail() never propagates, making the negative test vacuous; should use assertThrows instead

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the code uses `try { assertThat(driver.findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception ...) { /* expected */ }`. If the element exists, `assertThat(..., nullValue())` will throw an `AssertionError` (an `Error`, not an `Exception`), which is NOT caught by `catch (Exception)`, so the test will fail as intended. If the element does not exist, `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` (a `RuntimeException` → `Exception`), which is caught, also as intended. Therefore the assertion is not “vacuous” in the way described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError reads the auth note via Boolean.parseBoolean where the old code path used isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context), and the semantic equivalence of the extraction is unverified by unit tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior inline check `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler(...)` with `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, and the new utility method reads the auth note directly via `Boolean.parseBoolean(context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH))`. Since the implementation of `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` is not shown in the diff, it’s not verifiable here that this new extraction is semantically identical in all cases (e.g., if the old helper did more than parse the auth note). The added tests focus on passkey/reauth flows, but none explicitly asserts the re-auth form attributes controlled by this auth note, so equivalence of this refactor isn’t directly covered in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:113-115: webauthnAuth.fillContextForm moved out of the user==null branch and gated on isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) which requires user != null, inverting the condition so first-time unidentified users no longer get WebAuthn form data / passkey UI during initial login

UsernameForm.java:47: username form shown to every user when realm passkeys are enabled, without checking whether the re-authenticating user actually has a passkey credential, forcing password-only users through a username re-confirmation step with a failing passkey widget

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` to *not* skip the username form during re-authentication when passkeys/conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). There is no diff-shown check here (or in `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which only checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`) that the already-identified re-authenticating user actually has a passkey credential. So the finding’s core concern—conditional-passkeys gating is realm/feature-based rather than per-user-credential-based, potentially forcing password-only re-auth users through an extra username step—is grounded in the change. However, the claim that it affects “every user” and that it produces a “failing passkey widget” is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Divergent definitions of 'passkeys enabled' in sibling classes: UsernameForm uses no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() while UsernamePasswordForm uses isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) requiring non-null user, causing drift and inconsistent passkey UI between the two pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different “conditional passkeys enabled” checks being used in closely related authenticators: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` now gates behavior on `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg method, definition not shown here), while `UsernamePasswordForm` introduces `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` that additionally requires `user != null` (`return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;`). This is a concrete divergence in how “passkeys enabled” is determined across sibling pages and is a realistic source of future inconsistency/drift in passkey UI behavior, even if it may be intentional for now. The diff alone doesn’t prove a functional defect, but it does show the inconsistency in the conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only wired into two error paths (badPasswordHandler and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse), not other challenge() error renderings on the re-auth path, so the hidden-username attribute isn't re-applied and the username field reappears inconsistently

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the username-hiding logic was *moved* from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler()` into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` and is still invoked there, plus it was added to `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()`. The finding asserts there are other re-authentication error/challenge render paths where this should be applied, but no such additional error-rendering call sites are shown in the provided diff, nor is there evidence that any existing path lost the behavior (coverage appears increased, not decreased).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Realm-wide passkeys policy gate in UsernameForm.java disables the re-auth username-form skip for all users, including those without passkey credentials, causing a behavioral regression for password-only users

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate() from skipping the username form whenever context.getUser() != null to skipping only when context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(). This clearly alters re-authentication behavior based on a realm/feature-level passkeys gate (the method name implies it’s not per-user). However, from this diff alone we cannot verify that isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() ignores whether the current user actually has passkey credentials, nor that this necessarily causes a regression for password-only users; it is a plausible concern but not definitively a broken behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys policy instead of testing the enabled-realm + credential-less-user combination, hiding the regression

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the realm is explicitly configured with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` and the assertions verify that the WebAuthn form (`//form[@id='webauth']`) is absent during login and re-authentication. This does not exercise the scenario “passkeys enabled at realm level but the current user has no passkey credentials”, so it won’t catch regressions specific to that combination. However, the test’s own comment states it is intentionally covering “passkeys feature enabled, but passkeys is not enabled for the realm”, so it’s more a coverage/naming/scope concern than a verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: fillContextForm is now invoked with a non-null user through a code path (else branch of WebAuthnAuthenticator) written for the unidentified-user case, and the else branch may derive the username from login_hint rather than the re-authenticating user, rendering the wrong/blank username

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm gate the “user identified” branch on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) instead of (user != null). WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to always return false, while UsernamePasswordForm now calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) only when context.getUser() != null (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled). This means fillContextForm can be invoked with a non-null context.getUser() but will take the non-identified-user branch. The finding’s specific claim about that branch deriving username from login_hint/wrong username isn’t shown in this diff, but the control-flow mismatch is real and worth review for unintended side effects (e.g., username rendering/attributes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the enabled-passkeys + identified-user + no-passkey-credential rendering path for fillContextForm

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/relies on the “identified user” branch in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` via `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` (now defaulting to `context.getUser() != null`) and then builds `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` and checks `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty()` (i.e., a distinct rendering path when the user is identified but has no WebAuthn credentials). The added tests cover: passkeys enabled with users who do have passkeys (successful login/reauth), and a reauth case with passkeys disabled at the realm (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`). None of the new/modified tests exercise the case where passkeys are enabled in the realm, the user is already identified (reauth flow), but the user has no passkey/WebAuthn credential and thus `fillContextForm` takes the “empty authenticators” path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthenticatorUtils.java reimplements inline the logic of isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, creating two parsers of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note with no single source of truth, risking silent divergence if the note's semantics change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new parser of the auth note in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError()` (`context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH)` + `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`). The removed code in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler()` previously delegated to `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)`, implying similar logic exists elsewhere. The new util method does not reuse that existing helper, so the note semantics are now encoded in (at least) this new location, creating a maintainability/single-source-of-truth concern rather than a directly verifiable functional bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm.java:47 gates skipping the username form on realm-wide isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() rather than on the user actually having a passkey, so password-only users in passkeys-enabled realms get an extra re-auth step

adjudication.rationale: In UsernameForm.authenticate the skip condition changed from `context.getUser() != null` to `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, so in any scenario where conditional passkeys are enabled the username form will no longer be skipped even if the user is already identified (reauth). The diff does not show `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` checking whether the identified user actually has a passkey, so the reviewer’s concern (realm/feature-wide gating rather than per-user credential availability) is diff-grounded as a potential UX/scope regression, but the exact resulting behavior for password-only users can’t be fully verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test in the diff covers re-auth through UsernameForm for a password-only user

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes re-auth behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate()` by adding `&& !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` to the early-exit when `context.getUser() != null`. This alters the re-auth path specifically for flows using `UsernameForm` when conditional passkeys are enabled. The new/updated tests in the diff cover re-authentication for passkeys (e.g., `PasskeysUsernameFormTest#webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`) and password-only re-auth in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest#reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, but none clearly exercise the `UsernameForm` re-auth scenario for a password-only user (i.e., user already set + conditional passkeys enabled but no passkey). Given the logic change is in `UsernameForm`, the lack of a targeted test is a specific, diff-grounded gap rather than a generic "add tests" request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:63 shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() returning false unconditionally makes the inherited 2FA branch of fillContextForm (authenticator selection list) dead code for all instances, breaking pre-identified-user flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new hook `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` and overrides it in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` to return `false` with an explicit comment: "Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys". This does not make the 2FA branch dead code "for all instances"—only for this specific subclass. The change is intentional and scoped; other `WebAuthnAuthenticator` instances still use the default implementation (`return context.getUser() != null;`). From the diff alone, there's no verifiable break of pre-identified-user flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:197-201 silently reverses a previously accepted assertion (NoSuchElementException for the webauth form) to assert the form is present, changing the organizations flow's acceptance criteria without explicit maintainer sign-off

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest to assert the WebAuthn form is present where it previously asserted absence, but this aligns with the intentional behavior change in UsernamePasswordForm (now calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) i.e., user != null). The claim about “silently” changing acceptance criteria “without explicit maintainer sign-off” is not verifiable from the diff and isn’t a concrete defect or review issue grounded in the code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernamePasswordForm.java:113/137 inverts the fill condition from 'user not yet selected' to 'user selected', so realms without the WebAuthn passwordless execution in the browser flow silently lose conditional-UI form data on the username/password page

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() and challenge(error,field), the PR changes the condition for calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) from being allowed when the user is not yet selected (previously always in authenticate(), and explicitly `context.getUser() == null` in challenge()) to requiring `user != null` via isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user). As a result, on the initial username/password page render where `context.getUser()` is typically null, the WebAuthn conditional-UI/passkeys-related form attributes will no longer be populated, i.e., conditional-UI form data can be missing until after a user is identified (e.g., after a failed submit). The finding’s extra framing about “realms without the WebAuthn passwordless execution in the browser flow” isn’t directly provable from the diff, but the core regression (loss of fillContextForm when user is null) is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The UsernamePasswordForm coupling change is untested in the configuration without the co-resident WebAuthn execution

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a new hard coupling that would require a “co-resident WebAuthn execution”. In `UsernamePasswordForm`, all uses of `webauthnAuth` remain guarded: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly checks `webauthnAuth != null` before calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`, so a flow/configuration without any WebAuthn-related execution would simply result in `webauthnAuth == null` and skip the behavior. The finding asserts an untested scenario, but the diff does not establish that such a configuration is impacted or that a new dependency was introduced beyond optional behavior already guarded in code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication test does not assert the username form was rendered, so the regression fixed by the UsernameForm.authenticate change (skip only when !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) is invisible — the test passes green even if the behavior is reverted; same gap exists in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest's same-named test

adjudication.rationale: In both `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` and `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, the test flow goes straight from `oauth.openLoginForm()` / `prompt=login` to `appPage.assertCurrent()` and asserts only login events. There is no assertion that the username form (or any intermediate re-auth UI) was rendered/used, so these tests would likely still pass even if `UsernameForm.authenticate()` were reverted to the previous `if (context.getUser() != null) { context.success(); }` behavior. This is a concrete test-coverage gap tied to the new conditional skip logic (`context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse new error-path branch (setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError on passkey failure) has zero test coverage — no test simulates a failed passkey attempt during re-authentication

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` by calling `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` on the passkey-failure error path. The newly added/modified tests exercise re-authentication with `prompt=login` and also a failed *password* attempt (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`), but none of the added tests simulate a *failed WebAuthn/passkey* attempt during re-authentication that would drive execution through `createErrorResponse`'s failure branch. Therefore the finding about missing coverage for this new error-path logic is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey never asserts that the username input is hidden and registration is disabled, the two attributes the extracted AuthenticUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError exists to set — if the util silently no-ops the test still passes

adjudication.rationale: The diff extracts re-authentication form setup into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`, which sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is true. In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, the assertions after the failed password attempt only verify the error text (`"Invalid password."`) and that the WebAuthn form remains present; it does not assert that the username is hidden or registration is disabled. Therefore, if the new util method silently no-ops or regresses, this specific test would still pass, leaving the newly-centralized logic unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses an inverted try/catch assertion idiom where assertThat(..., nullValue()) is dead code and non-assertion exceptions (e.g., WebDriverException) are silently swallowed, passing the test without verifying anything — should use assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) instead; the idiom is duplicated twice

Inverted user-presence condition in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() (~113-117): isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, but conditional-UI fillContextForm must run when user == null (fresh login), so passkey autofill/conditional mediation is silently lost on the primary login path
matched_golden_ids: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires a non-null user, causing authenticate() to skip webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page when context.getUser() is null, which breaks conditional passkey UI/autofill for first-time (ID-less) passkey login—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same inverted gate in challenge() also prevents fillContextForm from being invoked on fresh login

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext,String,String)`, the condition to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` changed from `context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This is a direct inversion: on a fresh login where `context.getUser()` is null, `fillContextForm` will no longer be invoked from `challenge()`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator hard-returns false, causing fillContextForm in createErrorResponse to always take the anonymous path even when a user is identified, so the error-challenge page after a failed passkey during 2FA re-auth never shows the authenticator-selection list

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` now gates the “user identified / show authenticators list” branch on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)`, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides that to unconditionally return `false`. Therefore, when `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` calls `fillContextForm(context)`, it will not populate the available-authenticators list even if `context.getUser() != null`. However, the diff also includes an explicit comment in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` saying this is intentional (“Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”), and nothing in the diff proves that this authenticator is expected to show the selection list during 2FA re-auth flows. So the behavior change is real, but the claim that it is a definite broken 2FA re-auth scenario is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Nothing in code or logs distinguishes intentional suppression from lost authenticator list, making the behavior invisible to future maintainers changing error rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces an intentional suppression mechanism via `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` and an override in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` that returns `false` with a clear comment: "Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys". So the behavior is distinguishable in code (not “invisible”), and the finding’s claim that nothing distinguishes intentional suppression from a lost authenticator list is not supported by the diff.
